content: 1. The World Health Organization (WHO) has provided guidelines on the use of ferritin concentrations to assess iron status in both individuals and populations. These guidelines are detailed in Annex 6 of the document. 2. A systematic review was conducted to address the question: Is ferritin an adequate marker of iron stores, including the risk of deficiency and the risk of iron overload? This review is referenced in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews (2015; Issue 7: CD011817) and includes contributions from Garcia-Casal MN, Pasricha S-R, Martinez RX, Lopez-Perez L, and Peña-Rosas JP, affiliated with the World Health Organization in Geneva, Switzerland. 3. Another systematic review examined whether current serum and plasma ferritin cut-offs for diagnosing iron deficiency and overload are accurate and reflective of iron status. This review is published in Arch Med Res (2018; 49:405–417) and was authored by Garcia-Casal MN, Pasricha S-R, Martinez RX, Lopez-Perez L, and Peña-Rosas JP, also affiliated with the WHO. 4. A comprehensive overview of laboratory diagnosis for iron-deficiency anemia was published in J Gen Intern Med (1992; 7(2):145–153) by researchers from McMaster University, Ontario, Canada. 5. A systematic review focused on serum ferritin thresholds for diagnosing iron deficiency during pregnancy was published in Transfus Med (2017; 27(3):167–174) by researchers from Queen Mary University of London, United Kingdom. 6. The question of whether ferritin is an adequate marker for assessing the impact of iron interventions was addressed in a systematic review. This review summarized findings on ferritin concentration responses to nutrition-specific and nutrition-sensitive interventions in children and women of reproductive age. The review, submitted for publication in April 2019, is undergoing peer review. 7. A systematic review and meta-analysis explored the benefits of iron treatment in iron-deficient but non-anemic endurance athletes (IDNA). This study was published in Br J Sports Med (2015; 49(21):1389–1397) by researchers from St Mary’s University, Twickenham, United Kingdom. 8. Evidence from a systematic review and meta-analysis demonstrated improved micronutrient status and health outcomes in lowand middle-income countries following large-scale fortification programs. This study was published in Am J Clin Nutr (2019; 109(6):1696–1708) by researchers from the Centre for Global Child Health, Hospital for Sick Children, Toronto, Canada. 9. The question of how ferritin should be measured was addressed in a systematic review and meta-analysis evaluating the performance and comparability of laboratory methods for measuring ferritin concentrations in human serum or plasma. This study was published in PLoS One (2018; 13(5):e0196576) by researchers affiliated with the WHO. 10. The question of whether ferritin should be measured in combination with indicators of infection or inflammation was addressed in a meta-analysis. This study adjusted plasma ferritin concentrations to account for the effects of subclinical inflammation in assessing iron deficiency. It was published in Am J Clin Nutr (2010; 92:546–555) by researchers from the University of Ulster, United Kingdom. 11. Another study, part of the Biomarkers Reflecting Inflammation and Nutritional Determinants of Anemia (BRINDA) project, focused on adjusting ferritin concentrations for inflammation. This study was published in Am J Clin Nutr (2017; 106(Suppl. 1):359S–371S) by researchers from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), Georgia, United States. 12. The population prevalence ranges for determining a public health problem related to iron deficiency were explored in a study on the magnitude and distribution of iron deficiency across countries using serum/plasma ferritin. This study was published in Med Res Arch (2019; 7(12):2027) by researchers from the CDC. 13. The WHO guidelines on the use of ferritin concentrations to assess iron status in individuals and populations are further elaborated in Annex 7. It is noted that the acknowledgment of reviewers does not imply endorsement of the recommendations or represent the views, decisions, or policies of their affiliated institutions.
